report.rawText:
This confirms it: the `Books` model has no declared `__table_args__` index for `(owner_id, lower(title))` — the only index backing that access pattern existed solely as the standalone Alembic migration `b7c3e1f9a2d4`, which was dropped by `e2a9d4c1b6f8`. No replacement index exists.

## Diagnosis

**Root cause:** The migration `Schema cleanup: drop unused books title index` (commit `0ff1590`, applied 2026-07-26 20:55:50 UTC) dropped the composite index `ix_books_owner_lower_title` on `books(owner_id, lower(title))`. That index was not unused — it was the exact index backing `GET /v1/books` (`api/routes/books.py:186-271`), which filters `Books.owner_id == claim_id` and, by default (`sort_by=title`), orders by `func.lower(Books.title)`. With the index gone, every default-sorted books listing now falls back to a full table scan + sort (`ORDER BY lower(title)` with no supporting index), and this is the highest-traffic read endpoint in the app. The alert `BooklogrApiLatencyP99High` fired 46 seconds after the migration landed (20:56:36 UTC vs. 20:55:50 UTC drop), and Prometheus shows p99 latency is driven almost entirely by `/v1/books` (486ms) vs. `/` (5ms).

**Mechanism:** index removal → query planner can no longer do an index-ordered scan for `owner_id` + `lower(title)` → falls back to seq scan + sort → per-request latency increase on the most-hit endpoint → aggregate p99 crosses the 300ms threshold.

**Evidence**
- VALIDATED: `curl 'http://localhost:9093/api/v2/alerts'` — alert firing, `description: "p99 HTTP request latency is 491.8ms"`, `startsAt: 2026-07-26T20:56:36.403Z`.
- VALIDATED: `curl .../api/v1/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.99, ...by(le,path))` — `/v1/books` p99 = 0.486s, `/` p99 = 0.005s. The slow path is isolated to `/v1/books`.
- VALIDATED: `git show 36915c4` — index `ix_books_owner_lower_title` created on `books(owner_id, lower(title))`, comment: "Composite index backing the default library listing."
- VALIDATED: `git show 0ff1590` (timestamp 2026-07-26 20:55:50 UTC) — same index dropped, 46 seconds before the alert start time.
- VALIDATED: `api/routes/books.py:186-271` (`get_books`) — default `sort_by="title"`, query is `Books.query.filter(Books.owner_id==claim_id)...order_by(func.lower(Books.title))` — matches the dropped index's columns exactly.
- VALIDATED: migration chain walk (`down_revision` links) — `e2a9d4c1b6f8` (the drop) is the current head; no later migration re-adds an equivalent index. `api/models.py` Books model also declares no compensating index.
- INFERRED: actual query plan is now a sequential scan (could not confirm via `EXPLAIN` — no DB client available in this environment; inferred from index absence + endpoint-isolated latency spike).

**Recommended fix:** Revert/re-apply migration `b7c3e1f9a2d4` (recreate `ix_books_owner_lower_title` on `books(owner_id, lower(title))`) — i.e., roll forward with a new migration that re-adds the index rather than reverting history. The commit message's premise ("believed unused after the listing-query refactor") is false; `get_books` is still the primary consumer. Before dropping any index in the future, grep the actual query code (as done here) rather than relying on assumption/dead-code heuristics.

This confirms it: the `Books` model has no declared `__table_args__` index for `(owner_id, lower(title))` — the only index backing that access pattern existed solely as the standalone Alembic migration `b7c3e1f9a2d4`, which was dropped by `e2a9d4c1b6f8`. No replacement index exists.

## Diagnosis

**Root cause:** The migration `Schema cleanup: drop unused books title index` (commit `0ff1590`, applied 2026-07-26 20:55:50 UTC) dropped the composite index `ix_books_owner_lower_title` on `books(owner_id, lower(title))`. That index was not unused — it was the exact index backing `GET /v1/books` (`api/routes/books.py:186-271`), which filters `Books.owner_id == claim_id` and, by default (`sort_by=title`), orders by `func.lower(Books.title)`. With the index gone, every default-sorted books listing now falls back to a full table scan + sort (`ORDER BY lower(title)` with no supporting index), and this is the highest-traffic read endpoint in the app. The alert `BooklogrApiLatencyP99High` fired 46 seconds after the migration landed (20:56:36 UTC vs. 20:55:50 UTC drop), and Prometheus shows p99 latency is driven almost entirely by `/v1/books` (486ms) vs. `/` (5ms).

**Mechanism:** index removal → query planner can no longer do an index-ordered scan for `owner_id` + `lower(title)` → falls back to seq scan + sort → per-request latency increase on the most-hit endpoint → aggregate p99 crosses the 300ms threshold.

**Evidence**
- VALIDATED: `curl 'http://localhost:9093/api/v2/alerts'` — alert firing, `description: "p99 HTTP request latency is 491.8ms"`, `startsAt: 2026-07-26T20:56:36.403Z`.
- VALIDATED: `curl .../api/v1/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.99, ...by(le,path))` — `/v1/books` p99 = 0.486s, `/` p99 = 0.005s. The slow path is isolated to `/v1/books`.
- VALIDATED: `git show 36915c4` — index `ix_books_owner_lower_title` created on `books(owner_id, lower(title))`, comment: "Composite index backing the default library listing."
- VALIDATED: `git show 0ff1590` (timestamp 2026-07-26 20:55:50 UTC) — same index dropped, 46 seconds before the alert start time.
- VALIDATED: `api/routes/books.py:186-271` (`get_books`) — default `sort_by="title"`, query is `Books.query.filter(Books.owner_id==claim_id)...order_by(func.lower(Books.title))` — matches the dropped index's columns exactly.
- VALIDATED: migration chain walk (`down_revision` links) — `e2a9d4c1b6f8` (the drop) is the current head; no later migration re-adds an equivalent index. `api/models.py` Books model also declares no compensating index.
- INFERRED: actual query plan is now a sequential scan (could not confirm via `EXPLAIN` — no DB client available in this environment; inferred from index absence + endpoint-isolated latency spike).

**Recommended fix:** Revert/re-apply migration `b7c3e1f9a2d4` (recreate `ix_books_owner_lower_title` on `books(owner_id, lower(title))`) — i.e., roll forward with a new migration that re-adds the index rather than reverting history. The commit message's premise ("believed unused after the listing-query refactor") is false; `get_books` is still the primary consumer. Before dropping any index in the future, grep the actual query code (as done here) rather than relying on assumption/dead-code heuristics.

## Root Cause

**The migration `0ff1590` ("Schema cleanup: drop unused books title index") dropped the composite index `ix_books_owner_lower_title` on `books(owner_id, lower(title))`, which was actually load-bearing for the default `GET /v1/books` listing query.** Without it, Postgres now does a full sequential scan + sort over the entire `books` table (300k rows) on every request to the library listing endpoint, pushing p99 latency from comfortably under 300ms to ~490ms.

### Mechanism
- `api/routes/books.py:186` (`GET /v1/books`) defaults `sort_by="title"`, `order="asc"` (line 235-236) and always filters `WHERE owner_id = <claim_id>` (line 251).
- That produces exactly `... WHERE owner_id = ? ORDER BY lower(title) ASC` (line 264/267), which is precisely what `ix_books_owner_lower_title` was built to serve (see the index's own comment: *"Composite index backing the default library listing (owner-scoped, ordered by case-insensitive title)"*, added in commit `36915c4`).
- The drop migration's comment says the index was "believed to be unused after the listing-query refactor" — but the code still uses that exact filter+sort combination as the default path, so the belief was wrong.
- The drop was committed 2026-07-26 20:55:50 UTC; the alert started firing at 20:56:36 UTC — 46 seconds later, consistent with the migration being applied and traffic hitting the now-unindexed query almost immediately.

### Evidence

**VALIDATED:**
- `curl 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/query' --data-urlencode 'query=histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(flask_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, path))'` → `/v1/books` p99 = 0.4895s vs `/` = 0.0049s — isolates the slow path.
- `curl 'http://localhost:9093/api/v2/alerts'` → alert active, started `2026-07-26T20:56:36.403Z`.
- `git show 0ff1590` → migration `e2a9d4c1b6f8_drop_unused_books_title_index.py` drops `ix_books_owner_lower_title`, committed `2026-07-26 20:55:50`.
- `git show 36915c4` → the index was originally added specifically to back the owner-scoped, lower(title)-sorted listing query.
- `Read api/routes/books.py:224-271` → default query path is `Books.query.filter(owner_id==claim_id).order_by(func.lower(title).asc())`.
- `docker exec booklogr-db psql ... "\d books"` → only `books_pkey` remains; the composite index is confirmed absent in the live DB.
- `docker exec booklogr-db psql ... "select count(*) from books"` → 300,000 rows.
- `docker exec booklogr-db psql ... "EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT * FROM books WHERE owner_id = 1 ORDER BY lower(title) ASC LIMIT 25"` → `Seq Scan on books ... actual time=0.019..110.183 rows=300000` + `Sort` → **Execution Time: 201.671 ms** for this query alone, before app-level auth/serialization overhead — fully accounts for the observed ~490ms p99.

**INFERRED:**
- The remaining ~290ms beyond the raw SQL execution time (to reach the observed 490ms p99) is attributable to Flask request overhead, JWT auth (`@auth_required()`), and Marshmallow schema serialization (`BooksSchema(many=True).dump`) under load — not directly measured per-request here, but consistent with typical Flask/SQLAlchemy overhead.

### Recommended Fix
Re-create the dropped index via a new migration (do not resurrect/edit the reverted one):
```sql
CREATE INDEX ix_books_owner_lower_title ON books (owner_id, lower(title));
```
Given `sort_by` also accepts `author`, `rating`, `reading_status`, `isbn`, `created_on`, `progress` (line 224), consider whether those need supporting indexes too, but the default (`title`) is what's firing right now — restoring this one index should immediately resolve the alert.

## Root Cause

**The migration `0ff1590` ("Schema cleanup: drop unused books title index") dropped the composite index `ix_books_owner_lower_title` on `books(owner_id, lower(title))`, which was actually load-bearing for the default `GET /v1/books` listing query.** Without it, Postgres now does a full sequential scan + sort over the entire `books` table (300k rows) on every request to the library listing endpoint, pushing p99 latency from comfortably under 300ms to ~490ms.

### Mechanism
- `api/routes/books.py:186` (`GET /v1/books`) defaults `sort_by="title"`, `order="asc"` (line 235-236) and always filters `WHERE owner_id = <claim_id>` (line 251).
- That produces exactly `... WHERE owner_id = ? ORDER BY lower(title) ASC` (line 264/267), which is precisely what `ix_books_owner_lower_title` was built to serve (see the index's own comment: *"Composite index backing the default library listing (owner-scoped, ordered by case-insensitive title)"*, added in commit `36915c4`).
- The drop migration's comment says the index was "believed to be unused after the listing-query refactor" — but the code still uses that exact filter+sort combination as the default path, so the belief was wrong.
- The drop was committed 2026-07-26 20:55:50 UTC; the alert started firing at 20:56:36 UTC — 46 seconds later, consistent with the migration being applied and traffic hitting the now-unindexed query almost immediately.

### Evidence

**VALIDATED:**
- `curl 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/query' --data-urlencode 'query=histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(flask_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, path))'` → `/v1/books` p99 = 0.4895s vs `/` = 0.0049s — isolates the slow path.
- `curl 'http://localhost:9093/api/v2/alerts'` → alert active, started `2026-07-26T20:56:36.403Z`.
- `git show 0ff1590` → migration `e2a9d4c1b6f8_drop_unused_books_title_index.py` drops `ix_books_owner_lower_title`, committed `2026-07-26 20:55:50`.
- `git show 36915c4` → the index was originally added specifically to back the owner-scoped, lower(title)-sorted listing query.
- `Read api/routes/books.py:224-271` → default query path is `Books.query.filter(owner_id==claim_id).order_by(func.lower(title).asc())`.
- `docker exec booklogr-db psql ... "\d books"` → only `books_pkey` remains; the composite index is confirmed absent in the live DB.
- `docker exec booklogr-db psql ... "select count(*) from books"` → 300,000 rows.
- `docker exec booklogr-db psql ... "EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT * FROM books WHERE owner_id = 1 ORDER BY lower(title) ASC LIMIT 25"` → `Seq Scan on books ... actual time=0.019..110.183 rows=300000` + `Sort` → **Execution Time: 201.671 ms** for this query alone, before app-level auth/serialization overhead — fully accounts for the observed ~490ms p99.

**INFERRED:**
- The remaining ~290ms beyond the raw SQL execution time (to reach the observed 490ms p99) is attributable to Flask request overhead, JWT auth (`@auth_required()`), and Marshmallow schema serialization (`BooksSchema(many=True).dump`) under load — not directly measured per-request here, but consistent with typical Flask/SQLAlchemy overhead.

### Recommended Fix
Re-create the dropped index via a new migration (do not resurrect/edit the reverted one):
```sql
CREATE INDEX ix_books_owner_lower_title ON books (owner_id, lower(title));
```
Given `sort_by` also accepts `author`, `rating`, `reading_status`, `isbn`, `created_on`, `progress` (line 224), consider whether those need supporting indexes too, but the default (`title`) is what's firing right now — restoring this one index should immediately resolve the alert.
